faq.q: Why does rapid charging start slowly?
faq.a: For the first minute or so the car and charger check each other and the battery temperature, then ramp the power up. A cold battery may be held back until it warms.
asks: Why does a rapid charger take time to reach full power?

faq.q: Why is an empty battery quick to charge?
faq.a: In a nearly empty battery there is plenty of room for lithium ions to move into, and its voltage is low, so it can accept a big current safely.

faq.q: Why does charging slow down after 80 percent?
faq.a: Near full, the battery voltage approaches its safe limit and there is less room for lithium ions. To avoid overheating and damage, the car lowers the current, so charging slows a lot.
asks: Why does my electric car charge slowly at the end?

faq.q: Should I charge my electric car to 100 percent?
faq.a: For everyday driving, many makers suggest stopping around 80 percent, which is quicker and kinder to the battery. Charging to 100 is fine before a long trip.
asks: Is it bad to charge to full?

faq.q: Why does cold weather slow charging?
faq.a: In a cold battery the chemical reactions are slower, so pushing current in fast could damage it. The car limits power until the battery warms, and many cars pre-heat the battery on the way to a charger.
asks: Why is charging slower in winter?

facts: Rapid charging usually slows down sharply after about 80 percent charge.
Lithium-ion batteries are charged first at constant current, then at constant voltage while the current tapers off.
Many electric cars warm their battery before arriving at a rapid charger so it can charge faster.
